intro: The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard, and the Eagles will play on without Jalen Hurts after doctors found blood clots in his lungs. Tonight the Patriots visit the Bears on Prime Video, with Caleb Williams coming off a 305-yard return. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after a 2-4 start
top.dek: Indianapolis dismissed Ballard on Monday after ten seasons running the roster. Assistant GM Ed Dodds will oversee personnel while ownership searches for a replacement. Coach Shane Steichen and his staff now report to ownership.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts expected to miss the rest of the season
top.dek: Hurts has blood clots in his lungs and is on injured reserve, an AP source said. The team calls him clinically stable and expects a full recovery, but he cannot play until he is off blood thinners. Tanner McKee takes over for a 2-4 team on a four-game skid.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Bears CB Kyler Gordon records three sacks in 16 snaps
top.dek: Gordon played only 16 snaps in Atlanta and still finished with three sacks and a strip-sack. He is the first defensive back in the last 40 seasons with three sacks and multiple forced fumbles in one game.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 13: straight games the Cowboys have allowed 20 or more points
top.dek: Dallas owns the longest active streak in the NFL and the longest in franchise history. Green Bay converted 11 of 18 third downs against the Cowboys in Week 6. The defense gets Philadelphia on Monday night.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Patriots visit the Bears tonight on Prime Video
top.dek: Both teams are 4-2 for the Thursday night game at Soldier Field, kickoff 8:15 PM ET. Caleb Williams and Drake Maye, the top and third picks in 2024, meet for the second time. New England arrives with a pile of injuries on its offensive line.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit the bye with defensive questions

stories.text: Bills enter the bye with a defense that keeps bleeding points
stories.summary: Buffalo beat Las Vegas 33-30 on Sunday to reach 5-1, but the defense gave up another 30-point game. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson drew a one-game suspension for spitting at an opponent. The offense averages 32.8 points a game, tops in the NFL, and the November 10 trade deadline now looms over GM Brandon Beane.

stories.text: Bye gives Moore and Oliver about three weeks to heal
stories.summary: WR DJ Moore (shoulder) and DL Ed Oliver have each missed the last two games and returned to limited practice before the break. TE Dalton Kincaid and edge Bradley Chubb both hurt their ribs in Las Vegas, were listed questionable and came back. DB Jordan Hancock (calf) is on injured reserve and becomes eligible to return for the Ravens game.

stories.text: James Cook ran for 95 yards on 22 carries in Las Vegas
stories.summary: Cook has now topped 75 rushing yards in five straight games. He gained 62 of his yards after contact. His three runs of 10 or more yards give him 22 this season, the most in the league.

stories.text: 15: passing touchdowns the Bills defense has allowed
stories.summary: That is the second most in the NFL and the most through six games in a season since at least 2005. Buffalo has allowed 29 or more points in five of its six games. The Bills won all four games in which they gave up 30 or more.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Ravens at home Nov. 1
stories.summary: Buffalo is off this week and returns to host Baltimore on Sunday, November 1 at 1 PM ET on CBS. Watch how many of the injured starters return, and whether the secondary tightens up after the break.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins come off bye to face the Jets

stories.text: Winless Dolphins try to turn the bye into a reset
stories.summary: Miami is 0-5 and ranked 32nd in the NFL power rankings coming out of the break. Coach Jeff Hafley has talked about better discipline and fewer free yards and possessions. The Dolphins travel to the Jets on Sunday looking for their first win.

stories.text: Willis practiced fully on a sore thumb
stories.summary: QB Malik Willis was treated for a thumb injury on his throwing hand but practiced fully, and Hafley said he foresees Willis being good to go. WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) has not practiced since Week 2 and is questionable. RB Jaylen Wright had a setback with his foot against Cincinnati.

stories.text: Rookie Jacob Rodriguez set a Dolphins rookie record with 18 tackles
stories.summary: The linebacker's 18 tackles in the 15-10 loss at Minnesota on October 4 passed Zach Thomas's rookie mark of 16, set in 1996. Miami's defense also had four sacks, including two from Zach Sieler. The offense managed only eight first downs.

stories.text: 68.4: Malik Willis's passer rating through five starts
stories.summary: That ranks 29th in the NFL. Willis has two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns, four interceptions and five fumbles. He has said he has not played well enough.

stories.text: At the Jets on Sunday, 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami plays its first game since the Week 6 bye. Willis's thumb and Douglas's ankle are the two health questions to track. The Jets list several players on their own practice report, including running back Breece Hall.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots on short week at Chicago, line banged up

stories.text: Patriots play at Chicago tonight with their offensive line in pieces
stories.summary: New England has won three straight and sits 2-0 in the AFC East, but injuries from the 26-19 win over the Jets thinned the line. Coach Mike Vrabel said afterward his team did not play very well. The Bears are without suspended edge rusher Montez Sweat, and New England will test cornerback Jaylon Johnson with A.J. Brown.

stories.text: Both starting guards are out for Thursday night
stories.summary: Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee) are ruled out, along with cornerbacks Carlton Davis III (neck), Karon Prunty and Channing Canada (hamstrings). Tackle Morgan Moses (foot) was limited and is questionable. Safeties Kevin Byard III and Craig Woodson and linebacker Christian Elliss practiced fully and are questionable.

stories.text: Drake Maye threw three touchdowns for the third straight game
stories.summary: Maye went 18 of 32 for 235 yards and three scores against the Jets, with no interceptions and a 110.8 passer rating. His line allowed no sacks even as injuries forced changes. Receiver Romeo Doubs had a 42-yard touchdown before leaving with a shoulder injury.

stories.text: 3: straight games with three touchdown passes for Maye
stories.summary: He is the first Patriots quarterback to do that since Tom Brady in 2014. A.J. Brown's home debut was quiet by comparison: three catches on 10 targets for 27 yards.

stories.text: Tonight at Chicago, 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: New England plays the Bears at Soldier Field on a short week. Watch Maye's pocket against a Chicago pass rush playing without Sweat. The Patriots visit Miami on November 1 at 4:25 PM ET on CBS.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets need to finish drives and games

stories.text: Jets fall to 2-4 after a loss in New England that came down to finishing
stories.summary: The Jets trailed 17-3 at halftime and cut it to 23-13 but never completed the comeback. They failed on two fourth downs in the third quarter, and an offensive pass interference call wiped out a touchdown. Coach Aaron Glenn said the team has to fix finishing against good teams.

stories.text: Breece Hall sat out Wednesday with a quad injury
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall and rookie Kiko Mauigoa (quad) did not practice, and Glenn called Mauigoa and edge Joseph Ossai (ankle) week-to-week. Receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited, with pain tolerance a factor. Demario Davis and Harrison Phillips sat for veteran rest.

stories.text: Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. posted his first 100-yard game
stories.summary: Back from injured reserve after a Week 1 ankle injury, Cooper caught six passes for 103 yards and a 48-yard touchdown, his first in the NFL. He led the Jets in receiving. Braelon Allen added 78 yards on 17 carries.

stories.text: 166: attempts before Geno Smith threw his first interception
stories.summary: Smith finished 20 of 30 for 252 yards, one touchdown and that pick against New England. The Jets also went 0 for 3 in the red zone and 3 for 10 on third down.

stories.text: Dolphins visit Sunday, 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Jets host winless Miami. Hall's quad and the Jets' red-zone and third-down trouble are the things to watch.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens wait on Lamar Jackson's ankle

stories.text: Ravens look to bounce back from a 13-10 loss in Cleveland
stories.summary: Baltimore dropped to 4-2 after Cleveland's Deshaun Watson drove the Browns downfield for the winning field goal. Tyler Loop missed a 49-yard kick with the Ravens ahead in the fourth quarter, and coach Jesse Minter called the miss critical. Minter did not rule out signing another kicker, and the Ravens host the 3-2 Bengals on Sunday.

stories.text: Jackson returns to practice, limited, as Jurgens clears protocol
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson practiced in a limited role Wednesday for the first time since he hurt his ankle on Oct. 4. Minter called his status a day-by-day thing. Center Cam Jurgens cleared the concussion protocol and practiced fully, while outside linebacker Tavius Robinson (pectoral) joined the report and did not practice.

stories.text: Trey Hendrickson returns with eight pressures and a sack
stories.summary: The outside linebacker came back from a two-game finger absence against Cleveland and was one of the few bright spots for the defense. He faces his old team, the Bengals, on Sunday and practiced fully Wednesday. Minter said he was pleased with how Hendrickson handled the injury.

stories.text: 10 of 13: Tyler Loop's field goal ledger after the Cleveland miss
stories.summary: Loop has made 10 of 13 field goal tries this season, including a 56-yarder that won the Week 3 overtime game against Dallas. His miss from 49 yards came with Baltimore leading 10-3 early in the fourth quarter. A two-score lead could have forced the Browns to take more risks.

stories.text: Ravens host Bengals Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-2) hosts Cincinnati (3-2) in a division game coming off a loss. Watch whether Jackson or Tyler Huntley starts, and whether Jurgens makes his Ravens debut at center. Hendrickson against his former team adds another thread.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Rested Bengals visit Baltimore Sunday

stories.text: Bengals cannot afford a 0-2 division start, Burrow says
stories.summary: Cincinnati comes off its bye at 3-2 with the Ravens, Steelers and Browns all sitting at 4-2. Joe Burrow said an early division hole is not an option and called Baltimore the key matchup. The Bengals face the Ravens on Sunday in Baltimore.

stories.text: Bengals list only safety Kyle Dugger on Wednesday report
stories.summary: Dugger (quadricep) practiced on a limited basis, and he was the lone Bengals name on the Week 7 report. Receiver Colbie Young (knee) has missed three games and says he is ready to play Sunday. Final game designations come after Thursday and Friday practices.

stories.text: Joe Burrow arrives rested with 11 touchdowns through five games
stories.summary: Burrow has completed 71.4 percent of his passes for 1,361 yards and 11 touchdowns. Tight end Mike Gesicki already has four touchdown catches, so Baltimore cannot key only on Ja'Marr Chase. The Ravens want to disrupt Burrow's timing without thinning out their coverage.

stories.text: 155: rushing yards per game the Bengals have allowed in their last three
stories.summary: Cincinnati has leaked yards on the ground heading into a Baltimore game that features Derrick Henry. Henry leads the NFL with 130 carries and needs 111 yards to pass Jerome Bettis for eighth on the career list. He ran for a season-low 58 yards against Cleveland last week.

stories.text: Bengals at Ravens Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati opens a stretch of division play with a road trip to Baltimore. Watch how the Bengals handle Henry and whether Hendrickson, a Bengal for five seasons, finally sacks Burrow. He has never done so.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns ride Watson's late drives to 4-2

stories.text: Watson's fourth game-winning drive beats Baltimore
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson led the Browns to a 13-10 win over the Ravens, his fourth game-winning drive of 2026, tied with Bo Nix for most in the league. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger forced a fourth-quarter Derrick Henry fumble that Cleveland turned into the tying touchdown. The defense held Baltimore to 235 yards.

stories.text: Delpit, Schwesinger and Elgton Jenkins sit out Wednesday
stories.summary: Safety Grant Delpit (concussion), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle), guard Elgton Jenkins (knee) and defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) did not practice. Running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and receiver Denzel Boston (foot) were limited. Coach Todd Monken listed 16 players in all.

stories.text: Jerry Jeudy gets the game ball after a 69-yard day
stories.summary: Jeudy posted a season-high four catches, including a 33-yarder on third-and-5 with 42 seconds left that set up the winning kick. He has 12 catches for 150 yards this year after rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion took bigger roles. Jeudy said he stays focused day by day and declined to discuss trade talk.

stories.text: 24: sacks the Browns have allowed, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Cleveland's offensive line ranks 27th in pressure rate allowed, and Watson has been brought down more than any other quarterback. He still leads the league with three fourth-quarter comebacks. The Browns are 4-2 despite negative EPA per dropback.

stories.text: Browns at Titans Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cleveland visits Nashville to face Tennessee, which is 1-5 and has the league's lowest scoring offense. The Browns are 2-0 in the division. Watch the status of Judkins and Delpit, and whether the line can protect Watson.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers fly to Paris after OT rally

stories.text: Steelers erase a 13-point deficit to beat Tampa Bay in overtime
stories.summary: Pittsburgh trailed 16-3 and scored 23 unanswered points to win 26-19 at Tampa Bay. Aaron Rodgers called it a trajectory-altering win, and the Steelers are now 4-2. They head to Paris next for a Sunday morning game.

stories.text: Ramsey, Echols and Joseph-Day miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Cornerbacks Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and Brandin Echols (hamstring) and lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) did not practice. Running back Rico Dowdle (knee) and edge rusher Alex Highsmith (groin) were limited. T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward sat for rest and are expected to play.

stories.text: Rookie Germie Bernard catches 11 passes and the winning touchdown
stories.summary: Bernard finished with 11 catches for 87 yards and scored the game-winning touchdown in overtime at Tampa Bay. Fellow rookie Daylen Everette also picked off his first career pass. Jamel Dean intercepted Jalon Daniels and Jalen Ramsey sacked him on fourth down in overtime.

stories.text: 1992: last time Pittsburgh won after trailing by 13 entering the fourth
stories.summary: Per NFL Research, the Tampa Bay comeback was the first of its kind for the Steelers since 1992. It was the fourth such win of Rodgers' career. Pittsburgh outscored the Buccaneers 23-3 from there.

stories.text: Steelers face Saints in Paris Sunday at 9:30 AM ET on NFL Network
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays New Orleans at Stade de France in an early kickoff. Watch the health of the secondary, with Ramsey and Echols both held out Wednesday. The Steelers get a Week 9 bye after this game.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Tank Dell returns as Texans host Giants

stories.text: Tank Dell set to make his season debut against the Giants
stories.summary: Wide receiver Tank Dell practiced fully Wednesday and is on track to play Sunday, his first game since the knee injury that ended his 2024 season. Coach DeMeco Ryans said he expects Dell to play the offense the right way and just be himself. Houston arrives at 2-4 on a two-game winning streak after the 34-31 win over Jacksonville in London.

stories.text: Seven Texans sit out Wednesday practice, including Montgomery and Pitre
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin), safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder), safety Reed Blankenship (concussion and hand), linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (knee), tackles Trent Brown (wrist) and Blake Fisher (thumb) and tight end Dalton Schultz did not practice. Nico Collins and Will Anderson Jr. were limited for rest, while Jadeveon Clowney and Logan Hall were limited with knee issues. The team report lists participation only, so game statuses come later in the week.

stories.text: Foster Moreau scores twice before halftime in London
stories.summary: The tight end caught a touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud early and added a 1-yard score with eight seconds left in the second quarter. That second touchdown put Houston up 17-14 at the break. Moreau is a name to watch again if Schultz cannot go Sunday.

stories.text: 312: Stroud's passing yards in the win over Jacksonville
stories.summary: Stroud completed 24 of 34 passes for 312 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception in the end zone. Ka'imi Fairbairn then kicked a 49-yard field goal as time expired to win it. Neither team recorded a sack in the game.

stories.text: Giants visit Houston on Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Texans host New York in Week 7. Watch the Dell return and whether the injured safeties and Montgomery get back. The Giants have several defensive backs and offensive linemen sitting out early in the week.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts fire GM Ballard, face unbeaten Vikings

stories.text: Colts fire general manager Chris Ballard after 2-4 start
stories.summary: Indianapolis dismissed Ballard on Monday, his tenth season running the roster. Assistant GM Ed Dodds will oversee the personnel department while ownership searches for a replacement. Coach Shane Steichen and his staff now report to ownership, and the next three opponents are the 5-0 Vikings, the 4-2 Jaguars and the Cowboys.

stories.text: Sauce Gardner week to week with a calf strain
stories.summary: An MRI confirmed a mild strain in Gardner's left calf, and he is listed week to week. Tight end Tyler Warren (groin) missed the Titans game and linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) sat out as well, while receiver Anthony Gould entered the concussion protocol. Warren is described as progressing well.

stories.text: Daniel Jones keeps the job despite six interceptions
stories.summary: Steichen confirmed Jones starts Sunday at Minnesota and said he has to clean up the turnovers. Jones completes 59 percent of his passes at 5.9 yards per attempt with four touchdowns and six interceptions. The line struggled against Tennessee and the receiver group is thin without Alec Pierce.

stories.text: 10: straight losses to teams at .500 or better
stories.summary: The Colts also have dropped seven straight true road games. Both streaks meet an undefeated Vikings team Sunday that leads the league in takeaways. Steichen put the problems down to execution.

stories.text: Colts visit the 5-0 Vikings Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Indianapolis faces Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his blitz-heavy scheme. Jones spent time on the Vikings practice squad in 2024, which Steichen thinks helps this week's preparation. The Colts then travel to Jacksonville in Week 8.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars use bye to fix secondary, Thomas role

stories.text: Bye week arrives with Brian Thomas Jr. role in question
stories.summary: Jacksonville is 4-2 and on its Week 7 bye after the 34-31 loss to Houston in London. Thomas played only the first half after dropping an early pass, and Coen and Trevor Lawrence both said he needs more involvement. The trade deadline is a few weeks away, which adds pressure to settle his role.

stories.text: Secondary banged up heading into the bye
stories.summary: Cornerback Montaric Brown, Caleb Ransaw and Eric Murray have all missed time, and safety Antonio Johnson left the Houston game with an ankle injury in the third quarter. Brown and long snapper Ross Matiscik were ruled out before the London game. Current statuses are not yet public.

stories.text: Travis Hunter makes history with a catch and an interception
stories.summary: Hunter caught four passes for 59 yards and a 7-yard touchdown, then intercepted C.J. Stroud in the end zone. He is the first player with a receiving touchdown and an interception in one game since Brian Dawkins in 2002. He also played nine offensive snaps, a season high.

stories.text: 60: yards on Cam Little's game-tying field goal
stories.summary: Little's kick tied the game at 31 with 1:55 left, after Hunter's interception. Houston still had time and won on a 49-yard field goal as the clock expired. Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns in the loss.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Colts at home on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Jacksonville does not play for 11 days. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 1 against Indianapolis at 1 PM ET on CBS. The secondary and Thomas's role are the questions to watch.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans win first game, host Browns

stories.text: Saleh gets first win as Titans erase 13-point deficit
stories.summary: Tennessee beat Indianapolis 26-20 for its first victory of the season and Robert Saleh's first as head coach. The Titans trailed 13-0 at halftime and scored 26 second-half points, their most in a second half since 2020. The win was also the franchise's 500th.

stories.text: Adams, Ridley and Winston limited Wednesday
stories.summary: Safety Tony Adams (ankle), receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) and safety Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) were limited in the first practice of the week. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers and running back Tyjae Spears did not practice, listed as rest. Linebacker Dorian Mausi was a full participant with a foot issue.

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons wrecks the Colts with two sacks
stories.summary: Simmons recorded six tackles, two sacks and a forced fumble that he recovered himself. He now has 46.5 career sacks. The Titans as a team finished with six sacks, three takeaways and a blocked punt.

stories.text: 6: sacks, with no sacks allowed on offense
stories.summary: Tennessee paired six sacks with three takeaways and a blocked punt against Indianapolis. The team says no NFL club had put up that combination in 2026 before Sunday. Cam Ward went 11 of 22 for 102 yards and a touchdown behind a line that gave up zero sacks.

stories.text: Browns visit Nissan Stadium Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Tennessee has not won back-to-back games since November 2022, and a win over Cleveland would end that run. The defense that sacked Daniel Jones six times is the model for this week. Watch the health of the safety group, with Adams and Winston both limited.

source.name: Titans On SI via Yahoo Sports

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos win ugly in OT, face Cardinals

stories.text: Broncos escape Seattle in overtime, 17-14
stories.summary: Denver beat the Seahawks 17-14 on Thursday night to improve to 4-2. Wil Lutz won it with a 53-yard field goal in overtime, and the defense picked off Sam Darnold twice. The offense sputtered, and Bo Nix said he could not pinpoint why the big plays stopped coming.

stories.text: Surtain back at practice, Hufanga and Badie sit out
stories.summary: Cornerback Pat Surtain II returned to limited practice Wednesday for the first time since a Week 4 ankle injury. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), running back Tyler Badie (thumb) and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) did not practice. Payton said Elliss's injury should not end his season, and back Jonah Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve.

stories.text: Lutz nails 53 yards to beat Seattle
stories.summary: Kicker Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard field goal in overtime after Nix moved Denver into range. J.K. Dobbins added 17 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown, and R.J. Harvey scored on a wildcat run. Kris Abrams-Draine took away the Seahawks' last chance in regulation with an interception in the final minute and a half.

stories.text: 107: Passing yards for Nix in the Seattle win
stories.summary: Bo Nix went 17 of 27 for 107 yards against Seattle, about 4 yards per attempt. Sean Payton pointed to the offensive line and a more balanced run game as the fixes. Denver still won with two interceptions of Darnold, who threw 51 times.

stories.text: Broncos at Cardinals, Sunday 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver plays at Arizona after a mini-bye, with a chance to stretch its win streak to three. Payton wants cleaner detail work, a better run game and more from the offensive line. Kansas City visits Denver the following week.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs unbeaten, Walker keeps rolling

stories.text: Chiefs hit 5-0, the AFC's last unbeaten team
stories.summary: Kansas City beat the Chargers 22-6 and sits alone as the AFC's only undefeated team. Kenneth Walker ran for 128 yards and two touchdowns, and the defense logged four sacks after three weeks without one. The Chiefs are 3-0 in the division.

stories.text: Moore in concussion protocol, Rice still out
stories.summary: Right tackle Jaylon Moore did not practice Wednesday after leaving the Chargers game at halftime with a concussion, and Joshua Ezeudu is expected to start in his place. Receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) also sat out and has missed time since Week 4. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who has a bulging disc in his back, was expected to practice in some capacity.

stories.text: Walker keeps piling up explosive runs
stories.summary: Kenneth Walker carried 19 times for 128 yards and two scores against the Chargers, including a 33-yard run. It was his league-leading seventh run of 20 or more yards this season. He had 537 rushing yards through Week 4, the most by any player since 2010.

stories.text: 4: Sacks for Kansas City after a three-week drought
stories.summary: The Chiefs sacked the Chargers four times. Ashton Gillotte, George Karlaftis and Chamarri Conner had one each, and Peter Woods and Chris Jones split one. Los Angeles gained only 259 yards on 63 plays and never reached the end zone.

stories.text: Chiefs at Seahawks, Sunday 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Kansas City heads to Seattle for Sunday Night Football, then plays at Denver. The Seahawks' run game has looked weak without Walker, who left Seattle to join the Chiefs. A road stretch follows through Atlanta, Buffalo, Los Angeles and Cincinnati.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders score, but lose a third straight

stories.text: Raiders drop a third straight, 33-30 to Bills
stories.summary: Las Vegas fell to 3-3 after a 33-30 loss at the Bills, its third defeat in a row. Two of the three losses came by three points. The offense is not the problem: the Raiders average 27.0 points per game, sixth in the league, after finishing last at 14.3 in 2025.

stories.text: Bowers limited with hamstring and calf issues
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers (hamstring and calf), tackle Kolton Miller (shoulder), linebacker Quay Walker (chest) and running back Mike Washington (foot and back) were limited Wednesday. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (concussion) did not practice. Carter Runyon and Dont'e Thornton Jr. returned to practice from injured reserve.

stories.text: Tre Tucker goes for 97 and two scores
stories.summary: Receiver Tre Tucker caught five passes for 97 yards and two touchdowns against Buffalo, including a 44-yard score. It was his second game this season with at least 90 yards and two touchdowns. Tight end Michael Mayer also set a career high with 95 yards on seven catches.

stories.text: 14: Touchdown passes for Kirk Cousins, tied for the league lead
stories.summary: Cousins threw for 313 yards and two touchdowns against the Bills. His 14 touchdown passes match Trevor Lawrence for the most in the NFL. Las Vegas has 155 points through six games, its most since 2022.

stories.text: Raiders host Rams, Sunday 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas returns home to face Los Angeles in Week 7, looking to end the skid. Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) and linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) did not practice Wednesday. Watch the Raiders' run game, which averaged 3.25 yards per carry against Buffalo.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers weigh offensive changes

stories.text: Chargers start 0-6, Harbaugh to review everything
stories.summary: Los Angeles lost 22-6 at Kansas City to fall to 0-6. Jim Harbaugh said he will look at everything on offense, starting with himself, and did not commit to Mike McDaniel continuing to call plays. The offense ranks last in the NFL in EPA per play and averages 15.0 points per game.

stories.text: Line and receiver injuries pile up in Los Angeles
stories.summary: Ahead of the Chiefs game, left tackle Joe Alt (neck), safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring) and receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) did not practice. Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston (chest) were limited. Center Tyler Biadasz, tackle Rashawn Slater and tight end David Njoku are on injured reserve. This report is from last week, and the bye means no new designations this week.

stories.text: Cam Hart picks off Mahomes in the end zone
stories.summary: Cornerback Cam Hart intercepted Patrick Mahomes in the end zone, and Mahomes finished without a touchdown pass for the first time this season. The Chargers defense ranks 12th in EPA per play. Derius Davis also had a season-long 21-yard punt return.

stories.text: 0-6: First Chargers start that bad since 2000
stories.summary: The Chargers are the first 0-6 team in the NFL since the 2000 Chargers, who went 1-15. Harbaugh played on that team. Los Angeles holds the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft by current standings.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Rams on Nov. 1
stories.summary: The Chargers rest this week and return Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:05 PM ET on Fox against the Rams at SoFi Stadium. The open week gives Harbaugh time to decide on the offense and play-calling.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Dak faces a blitz test in Philly

stories.text: Prescott's blitz problem follows Dallas to Philadelphia
stories.summary: Dak Prescott threw two interceptions and one touchdown against a Green Bay defense that blitzed on 35.71 percent of his dropbacks. Film review of the Tampa Bay game showed his EPA per play fell from +0.09 without a blitz to -0.31 against one. Eagles coordinator Vic Fangio does not blitz often, but Dallas expects him to send extra rushers Monday night.

stories.text: Overshown and Durant trend toward Monday returns
stories.summary: Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) has missed five games and expects to play against the Eagles. Cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) has missed four and is trending toward a return, per coach Brian Schottenheimer. KaVontae Turpin (rib cartilage) and Dee Winters (Achilles) are expected to miss time.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb carries the Dallas offense
stories.summary: Lamb has 69 targets, 48 catches, 577 yards and 4 touchdowns through six games. Dallas ranks eighth in offensive EPA per play, and he drives much of it. He now faces an Eagles pass defense that ranks 25th in EPA per pass.

stories.text: 13: straight games allowing 20 or more points
stories.summary: Dallas has given up at least 20 points in 13 straight games, the longest active streak in the NFL and the longest in franchise history. Green Bay converted 11 of 18 third downs in Week 6. Opponents are moving the chains on 54.67 percent of Dallas third-down snaps.

stories.text: At Eagles, Monday, 8:15 PM ET, ESPN
stories.summary: Dallas visits Lincoln Financial Field on Monday night with a 2-4 record, coming off two straight losses. Watch whether the Cowboys can slow a Philadelphia offense that ranks 31st in EPA per play. The Cardinals visit AT&T Stadium in Week 8.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: McCarthy gets the start in Houston

stories.text: Giants hand J.J. McCarthy the starting job
stories.summary: Coach John Harbaugh named McCarthy the Week 7 starter over Jameis Winston. McCarthy replaced Winston midway through the 34-27 loss to New Orleans and threw for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Harbaugh would not call him the long-term answer and said the job can change.

stories.text: Thomas, Edmunds and Holland sit out Wednesday
stories.summary: Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and safety Jevon Holland (concussion) did not practice Wednesday. Tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) also sat out. Thursday and Friday reports will set game statuses.

stories.text: Malik Nabers piles up 165 yards on 12 catches
stories.summary: Nabers caught 12 passes for 165 yards on 15 targets against the Saints. Tight end Isaiah Likely added six catches for 99 yards and his fifth touchdown of the year. The pair gives McCarthy two proven targets in his first start.

stories.text: 175: rushing yards the Giants gave up to New Orleans
stories.summary: The Saints ran 38 times for 175 yards in the Giants' Week 6 loss. Houston ranks 25th in rushing yards and 29th in yards per attempt, so the Giants have a chance to fix it. Running back Woody Marks has 205 yards at 3.5 per carry, and David Montgomery may miss the game.

stories.text: At Texans, Sunday, 1 PM ET, Fox
stories.summary: New York travels to Houston at 3-2-1, then goes on its Week 8 bye. The Texans are 2-4 and have won two straight. C.J. Stroud has 1,714 passing yards, nine touchdowns and one interception, and Will Anderson Jr. leads the league with 7.5 sacks.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Hurts is out as the losing streak hits four

stories.text: Hurts expected to miss the rest of the season
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts has blood clots in his lungs and is on injured reserve, an AP source said. The team says he is clinically stable and expects a full recovery, but he cannot play until he is off blood thinners. Philadelphia is 2-4 after a fourth straight loss, its first such streak since 2020.

stories.text: Barkley's return is in question for Monday
stories.summary: Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) missed two games and is listed questionable against Dallas. Edge rushers A.J. Epenesa, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith, along with Michael Carter II and Carson Steele, are also questionable. Landon Dickerson is on injured reserve, and Lane Johnson is on the reserve/retired list.

stories.text: Tanner McKee asks for more after his first start
stories.summary: McKee went 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown in the 25-14 loss to Carolina. In seven career games he has six touchdown passes and one interception. Coach Nick Sirianni says he has the utmost confidence in McKee, and Sean Mannion keeps the play-calling job.

stories.text: 218.5: yards per game during the four-game skid
stories.summary: The Eagles gained 248, 172, 232 and 222 yards in their four straight losses. Their 1.84 rushing average over the last two weeks matches their worst since 1955. They also have not scored a third-quarter touchdown this season.

stories.text: Vs. Cowboys, Monday, 8:15 PM ET, ESPN
stories.summary: Philadelphia hosts Dallas at Lincoln Financial Field, 2-4 and in need of a win. Watch Barkley's status and whether the line can open run lanes. Next comes a Week 8 trip to Washington on Sunday night.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: McLaurin out for the year heading into bye

stories.text: Commanders lose Terry McLaurin to a torn patellar tendon
stories.summary: McLaurin went down in the first quarter at San Francisco and left on a cart. Coach Dan Quinn announced Tuesday that the team captain is out for the season. Washington rallied from a 20-point deficit but lost 23-17, and now takes its bye week.

stories.text: Receiver depth shrinks without McLaurin
stories.summary: McLaurin leads the team with 230 receiving yards, and his season is over. Stefon Diggs steps into the top role, with Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams behind him. Tight end Chig Okonkwo should see more targets.

stories.text: Sonny Styles posts 13 tackles at San Francisco
stories.summary: The rookie linebacker led Washington with 13 tackles and a pass defensed against the 49ers. His four passes defensed are the most by a Commanders rookie since Ryan Kerrigan in 2011. Frankie Luvu added 8 tackles and a fumble recovery.

stories.text: 300: yards for Jayden Daniels against the 49ers
stories.summary: Daniels went 29 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns, his first 300-yard game since Week 8 of 2024. He is the first Washington quarterback to reach 300 on a Monday night since Case Keenum in 2019. Okonkwo caught 7 passes for 69 yards.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Eagles on Sunday night
stories.summary: Washington is off this week. The Commanders host Philadelphia in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. Quinn has the bye to rework the receiver room.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams is back for Patriots on Thursday

stories.text: Williams returns from hamstring injury with a 305-yard rebound
stories.summary: Caleb Williams came back after missing three games and completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown in a 31-23 win at Atlanta. Coach Ben Johnson called the layoff the longest injury absence of Williams' career. The Bears now host New England on Thursday night.

stories.text: Monangai and Sanborn out, Edwards doubtful vs. Patriots
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) and linebacker Jack Sanborn (concussion) are out. Linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring) is doubtful. Defensive back Tyrique Stevenson (hip) is questionable despite full practices, and guard Jonah Jackson is cleared.

stories.text: Kyler Gordon piles up three sacks in 16 snaps
stories.summary: Gordon returned to the defense and played only 16 snaps against Atlanta. He still recorded three sacks and finished the game with a strip-sack. He is the first defensive back in the last 40 seasons with three sacks and multiple forced fumbles in one game.

stories.text: 83.3%: Williams' completion rate in his return
stories.summary: Williams hit 30 of 36 throws against the Falcons, good for 83.3 percent and 305 yards. He is one of three quarterbacks in NFL history with at least 50 touchdown passes and 15 or fewer interceptions, joining Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson.

stories.text: Patriots at Soldier Field, Thursday night on Prime Video
stories.summary: Chicago hosts New England on Thursday, Oct. 22 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Both teams are 4-2. Williams and Drake Maye, the top and third picks in 2024, meet for the second time, and New England is dealing with a pile of injuries on its offensive line.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions off bye, with Packers at Ford Field

stories.text: Lions come off bye needing a defense fix before Packers and Vikings
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Green Bay on Oct. 25 and Minnesota on Nov. 1 after the bye. The offense is rolling, but the defense gives up a league-high 404.4 yards per game. The Lions sit last in the NFC North at 3-2.

stories.text: Branch and Mays expected back from long injuries
stories.summary: Safety Brian Branch (torn Achilles) and center Cade Mays (fractured wrist) are both expected to play, barring a setback, Dan Campbell said Monday. Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) was limited in an estimated Wednesday report after a walkthrough.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs runs toward a touchdown record chase
stories.summary: Gibbs has over 500 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns through five games. He is the first player since Christian McCaffrey in 2019 with 500 rushing and 240 receiving yards in that span. He says he wants LaDainian Tomlinson's single-season touchdown record of 31.

stories.text: 404.4: yards per game the Lions defense allows
stories.summary: Detroit allows a league-high 404.4 yards per game and ranks third-worst in scoring defense at 29.6 points. The figures run through five games. The pass rush is a bright spot with 20 sacks, and four players have at least three.

stories.text: Packers at Ford Field, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Green Bay on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. It is the Lions' first division game of the year. Watch whether the bye helps a defense that ranks 25th in DVOA against a Packers unit allowing 11.3 points per game.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers ride defense, Jacobs set to return

stories.text: Jacobs eligible to return Sunday at Detroit
stories.summary: The NFL removed running back Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list, and he can play again Oct. 25 at Detroit. He was placed on the list Aug. 30 after charges tied to a May arrest, and he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage. The league's personal conduct investigation continues. Green Bay ranks last in rushing.

stories.text: Love limited with sore back, receivers dinged
stories.summary: Quarterback Jordan Love was limited Wednesday with a sore back after being hit eight times against Dallas, and he said he is not worried about playing. Wide receivers Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams were also limited, and Bo Melton (back) did not practice.

stories.text: Evan Williams and rookie Cisse feed a takeaway machine
stories.summary: Evan Williams made a key second-quarter interception against Dallas, and Brandon Cisse picked off his first career pass. The defense has nine interceptions through six games. Micah Parsons is still a few weeks from his season debut after a torn left ACL.

stories.text: 11: takeaways, tied for the NFL lead
stories.summary: Green Bay has 11 takeaways, tied with Seattle for the most in the league, and nine interceptions. The Packers have held three straight opponents to 14 points or fewer, something they had not done since before Matt LaFleur arrived in 2019.

stories.text: At Lions, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Green Bay visits Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch Jacobs in a rushing offense that averages 59.8 yards per game, and Love's health. The Packers then host Carolina on Thursday night in Week 8.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings get healthy off the bye

stories.text: Undefeated Vikings return from bye to host Colts
stories.summary: Minnesota is 5-0 and gets Indianapolis (2-4) at home on Sunday after the bye. Four players returned to full practice Wednesday. Kevin O'Connell said the return of the group could put the team in a bit more of an attack mode.

stories.text: Darrisaw, Hockenson, Addison and Mason back at full practice
stories.summary: Left tackle Christian Darrisaw, tight end T.J. Hockenson, receiver Jordan Addison and running back Jordan Mason all practiced fully Wednesday. Tackle Brian O'Neill (knee), cornerback James Pierre (foot) and receiver Justin Jefferson (ankle) were limited. Game designations come Friday.

stories.text: Justin Jefferson has 258 yards and 3 touchdowns
stories.summary: Jefferson has 19 catches for 258 yards and three touchdowns, and he has worked through a nagging ankle injury that he says is improving daily. He was limited early this week. Kyler Murray is throwing him the ball.

stories.text: 68.3%: Kyler Murray's completion rate
stories.summary: Murray has completed 68.3 percent of his passes for 662 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He has also run 20 times for 93 yards. Those numbers come through his fifth start.

stories.text: Colts at home, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Indianapolis on Sunday, Oct. 25 at noon CT, which is 1 p.m. ET, on CBS. The Colts are 2-4 and just fired GM Chris Ballard. Indianapolis leads the all-time series 18-9-1, but the Vikings won the last two meetings.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons chase answers after a second straight loss

stories.text: Falcons dig out of a 31-7 hole, but the loss to Chicago still stings
stories.summary: Atlanta fell behind Chicago 31-7 before a fourth-quarter rally made the final 31-23. The Falcons are 2-4 and have lost two straight at home. Pass protection and two quick three-and-outs to open the game drew the loudest criticism, and now the 49ers visit on Sunday.

stories.text: Rookie LB Kendal Daniels practices fully, A.J. Terrell returns to practice
stories.summary: Daniels, carted off with a neck injury against the Bears, took part fully on Wednesday and is not in the concussion protocol. Cornerback A.J. Terrell, on injured reserve since Week 2, practiced on a limited basis, which starts a 21-day window for the team to activate him. Linebacker Divine Deablo and Billy Bowman Jr. did not practice.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson gets only nine carries for 61 yards against Chicago
stories.summary: Robinson ran nine times for 61 yards in the loss, about 6.8 yards a carry, while the Falcons spent most of the game chasing points. Defenses keep loading the box against him. A bigger share of touches against San Francisco would help the offense get back to its base plays.

stories.text: 31-7: the deficit Atlanta faced before its comeback attempt
stories.summary: Chicago built a 31-7 lead, and the Falcons outscored the Bears 16-0 the rest of the way. That rally came too late to matter. Atlanta now faces a 49ers team with Brock Purdy tied for the league lead with 14 passing touchdowns.

stories.text: Falcons host the 49ers Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Atlanta hosts San Francisco at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Watch whether Robinson gets going on the ground and whether the line keeps Michael Penix Jr. clean. Terrell's possible activation from injured reserve would help a thin cornerback group.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers hold the division lead before Tampa visit

stories.text: Panthers run past the Eagles 25-14 and sit atop the NFC South
stories.summary: Carolina controlled the ball for 34:48 and beat Philadelphia 25-14 on the road to move to 3-2. The defense held the Eagles to 35 rushing yards and sacked the quarterback three times. The Panthers now host Tampa Bay on Sunday with a chance to build on the division lead.

stories.text: Jaelan Phillips expected to miss Sunday with a hamstring injury
stories.summary: Phillips hurt his hamstring in Week 4, tweaked it again in the first quarter against the Eagles, and did not practice Wednesday. Coach Dave Canales said the MRI calls for more intensive treatment and Phillips is expected to sit against Tampa Bay. Pat Jones II and Princely Umanmielen should see more snaps, and outside linebacker Thomas Incoom also missed practice with a calf issue.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard carries 28 times for 120 yards and a score
stories.summary: Hubbard did the heavy lifting in Philadelphia, including a 19-yard run on fourth-and-1 that set up his one-yard touchdown. Tommy Tremble caught two touchdowns and Bryce Young threw for 281 yards with no interceptions. Hubbard sat out Wednesday's practice for rest.

stories.text: 399-222: Carolina's yardage edge over Philadelphia
stories.summary: The Panthers out-gained the Eagles 399 to 222, ran 25 first downs to 17 and never turned the ball over. Philadelphia was without Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley. The clean game gave Carolina its second straight win.

stories.text: Panthers host the Buccaneers Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Tampa Bay may get Baker Mayfield back from a thumb injury, and rookie Jalon Daniels starts if he cannot go. Carolina's pass rush has to get to the quarterback without Phillips. Keep Bryce Young clean and slow down Bucky Irving.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints head to Paris after snapping a skid

stories.text: Saints beat the Giants 34-27 and fly to Paris to face Pittsburgh
stories.summary: New Orleans snapped a three-game losing streak against New York and now seeks its first winning streak of the year. The Saints play Sunday at Stade de France, their first international game since 2022. They have a Week 8 bye, then two home games at the Superdome.

stories.text: Tyler Shough plays with broken bones in his non-throwing hand
stories.summary: Shough has thrown 12 touchdowns and five interceptions through six games, and Yahoo ties his recent drop in passing yards to the hand injury. Wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is recovering from a hamstring injury and traveled with the team, so a debut is possible. The team had not posted its official Week 7 report when that preview ran.

stories.text: Martin Emerson Jr. named NFC Defensive Player of the Week
stories.summary: Emerson intercepted Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy, broke up four passes and made seven solo tackles against the Giants. Those two picks matched his career best. He has two interceptions and four pass breakups through five games with New Orleans.

stories.text: 175: season-best rushing yards in the win over New York
stories.summary: The Saints ran for 175 yards against the Giants, their best total of the season, even after guard Cesar Ruiz left in the second quarter. Rookie Jeremiah Wright stepped in and allowed one pressure. The unit now meets a Pittsburgh run defense ranked 14th in the league.

stories.text: Saints face the Steelers in Paris Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
stories.summary: New Orleans allows 29.7 points a game, and Pittsburgh brings Aaron Rodgers to Stade de France. The Saints have the all-time series lead at 9-8 and then rest in Week 8. Watch the run defense, which ranks 30th at 138.0 yards a game.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs blow a 16-3 lead; Mayfield back at practice

stories.text: Bucs squander a 16-3 lead and lose 26-19 to Pittsburgh in overtime
stories.summary: Pittsburgh scored on four straight fourth-quarter drives, and Chase McLaughlin's 53-yard kick tied it with eight seconds left before Aaron Rodgers won it in overtime. Tampa Bay is 1-5. Todd Bowles said the team has no margin for error and must learn to finish games.

stories.text: Baker Mayfield returns to practice with a dislocated thumb healing
stories.summary: Mayfield has been out since Week 3 and appeared on Wednesday's report as a full participant, with the team's wording saying right thumb. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion and foot), tackle Luke Goedeke, running back Bucky Irving and cornerback Zyon McCollum did not practice. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. was limited with a rib injury.

stories.text: David Walker piles up two sacks in the loss
stories.summary: Walker recorded two sacks, five tackles and three quarterback hits against Pittsburgh. It was the first two-sack game by a Buc since October 2025. Rookies Rueben Bain Jr. and Keionte Scott each got their first career sacks.

stories.text: 48: Josiah Trotter's tackles through five games
stories.summary: Trotter's 48 tackles are the most by a Buccaneer through his first five games since at least 2000. He added 11 tackles and a pass deflection against the Steelers. Tampa Bay held Pittsburgh to 144 yards through three quarters.

stories.text: Bucs visit the Panthers Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Tampa Bay goes to Charlotte with Mayfield's status the main question. Rookie Jalon Daniels has thrown 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions in three starts. The Bucs play Atlanta in Week 8, then have their bye in Week 10.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Ryland's kick stuns Rams, ends skid

stories.text: Cardinals steal one in L.A. on Ryland's final kick
stories.summary: Chad Ryland hit a 43-yard field goal as time expired to give Arizona an 18-16 win over the Rams. The Cardinals were double-digit underdogs and snapped a four-game losing streak. It was Arizona's first NFC West win after eight straight divisional losses, and the second win of Mike LaFleur's career as head coach.

stories.text: Love misses Wednesday practice again with ankle
stories.summary: Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice Wednesday, the third week in a row he has been out of the first session. His ankle has bothered him since Week 4 against the Giants, and he sat out the Rams game. Safety Budda Baker (groin and illness) also sat out, along with six other Cardinals.

stories.text: Ryland goes 6-for-6 and carries the offense
stories.summary: Kicker Chad Ryland made all six of his field goal tries against the Rams, including the 43-yarder at the gun. Arizona scored on six of its 10 drives, and every score was a field goal. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett threw for 218 yards and kept drives moving without a touchdown pass.

stories.text: 0: touchdowns in a Cardinals win
stories.summary: Arizona went 0-for-5 in the red zone and still beat the Rams. It was the franchise's first win without a touchdown since a 12-7 win over the Titans in Week 14 of 2017. Both of the Cardinals' wins this season have come at SoFi Stadium.

stories.text: Cardinals host Broncos Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona hosts Denver in Week 7. Watch the practice reports for Love and Baker, and whether the offense can finish red zone drives with touchdowns. The Broncos are 4-2.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams lose again, fourth kicker search starts

stories.text: Rams fall to 2-4 after a flat loss to Arizona
stories.summary: Los Angeles lost 18-16 at home as double-digit favorites. The offense scored one touchdown through the first 59 minutes, and a questionable roughness call on Josh Wallace helped set up the winning kick. Coach Sean McVay said the problems start with him.

stories.text: Grupe tears ACL, Rams sign McManus
stories.summary: Kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL tackling a kickoff returner and went on injured reserve Monday. The Rams signed Brandon McManus, their third kicker of the season. They also list receiver Davante Adams (ruptured hamstring, six to 10 weeks) and nose tackle Poona Ford (season-ending triceps) on injured reserve.

stories.text: Stafford absorbs a beating and still throws for 222
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford finished 25 of 33 for 222 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. He took three sacks and five more hits, and lost a fumble with no one near him. Most of his production came on the final drive, when the Rams went 86 yards for a 16-15 lead.

stories.text: 4.2: yards per attempt for Stafford against Arizona
stories.summary: Stafford averaged just 4.2 yards per pass despite the 25-for-33 line. Before the late rally he was 18 of 26 for 137 yards. The Rams produced few explosive plays and the defense recorded no sacks or takeaways after the first drive.

stories.text: Rams visit Raiders Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles travels to Las Vegas for a game against the 3-3 Raiders, who are led by first-year coach Klint Kubiak and quarterback Kirk Cousins. McManus will kick for the Rams for the first time. Watch how the offense replaces Adams in the red zone.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers hold on to stay perfect

stories.text: 49ers survive Washington rally to reach 6-0
stories.summary: San Francisco beat the Commanders 23-17 on Monday night and sits atop all five national power rankings. The Niners built a 20-3 halftime lead, then watched Washington score the final 14 points. It is the second 6-0 start of Kyle Shanahan's tenure, after 2019.

stories.text: Evans questionable, Bosa and Samuel out for Atlanta
stories.summary: Receiver Mike Evans left the Washington game with Achilles tendinitis and is listed questionable. Defensive end Nick Bosa, receiver Deebo Samuel and linebacker Garret Wallow are out. Shanahan said the Evans injury is not believed to be a long-term problem.

stories.text: Purdy sits in the MVP race
stories.summary: Brock Purdy has completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 1,460 yards, 14 touchdowns and two interceptions. That puts him in a close MVP race with Josh Allen. San Francisco is the last undefeated team in the NFC.

stories.text: 56: Monday night wins, the most in NFL history
stories.summary: The win over Washington was San Francisco's 56th on Monday Night Football. That passes the Pittsburgh Steelers for the most in league history. The Niners now go on the road on a short week for their first East Coast trip of the year.

stories.text: 49ers visit Falcons Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: San Francisco plays at Mercedes-Benz Stadium against the 2-4 Falcons. Watch the injury report for Evans and whether the Niners close out a game after nearly giving away a 17-point lead against Washington.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks regroup before Chiefs on Sunday night

stories.text: Darnold takes the blame after overtime loss
stories.summary: Seattle lost 17-14 in overtime to Denver on Thursday night, and two Sam Darnold interceptions led to the defeat, one setting up Denver's winning field goal. Darnold said the offense must improve across the board and that it starts with him. The Seahawks are 3-3 and trail the 6-0 49ers by three games.

stories.text: Charbonnet back at full practice, four LBs sit
stories.summary: Running back Zach Charbonnet practiced fully Wednesday and has a chance to come off the physically unable to perform list this week. Guard Anthony Bradford returned to practice and will play if he looks good, per Mike Macdonald. Linebackers Connor O'Toole, Chazz Surratt and Drake Thomas did not practice, and DeMarcus Lawrence got a rest day.

stories.text: Smith-Njigba keeps piling up catches
stories.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 passes for 134 yards against Denver. Through six games he has 49 receptions, 717 yards and seven touchdowns. He is the clear top target in an offense that lacks a second dependable option.

stories.text: 14: sacks on Darnold in five games
stories.summary: Darnold has gone down 14 times in five games, and the pass protection has slipped from last season's level. The run game is a bigger problem: Seattle ranked last in rush EPA entering Week 7. Both numbers are the main reasons the offense has stalled.

stories.text: Seahawks host unbeaten Chiefs Sunday at 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Seattle gets a prime-time home game against Kansas City, which is 5-0. Watch the run game and whether Charbonnet and Bradford return. The Seahawks then host the Bears next week before facing the Cardinals in Week 9.
